results.title: A short story about why hiring in 2026 is broken. | Anya Storozhenko
results.content:
an extreme example - but misconfigured sourcing tools can quietly damage your hiring pipeline for months while everyone assumes the market is just tough. And for candidates: if you’re not getting interviews for roles you’re clearly qualified for, it may genuinely not be you. Which is a frustrating thing to sit with. Have you ever been rejected from a role that felt like a near-perfect match? 👇 [...] + applied to my own company's job posting under a fake name. rejected in 6 minutes.
    I lead a team of nine. We've had a desperate need for a senior associate role since april and hr keeps telling me the pipeline was thin, nothing passing screening. So last month i made a new email, changed my name, tweaked the dates, and applied to my own req with essentially my own cv. The CV of the person who wrote the job description and brother i was auto-rejected in six minutes!
    Took a week to work out why. the filter was set to require React.js and my cv says React. that's it. that's the whole thing, a full stop.
    We have been rejecting every qualified applicant since april over punctuation, while i sat in weekly meetings being told the market was tough. [...] A short story about why hiring in 2026 is broken. A hiring manager at a well known startup applied to his own job opening under a fake name. The ATS rejected him in 6 minutes. The story went viral. 9.2 million people saw it on X. Here’s what likely happened.
